discovery: Trapping and precision measurement of cold antimatter, testing CPT symmetry

nominees.name: Stefan Ulmer
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN, Japan / Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision fundamental-symmetry tests
motivation: Why the universe contains matter but almost no antimatter is one of the deepest open questions in physics. These three physicists made antimatter a subject of precision laboratory metrology. Gabrielse pioneered the capture and cooling of antiprotons in Penning traps, making cold antihydrogen possible and the first precise antiproton charge-to-mass comparisons feasible. His single-particle techniques also produced the most precise electron magnetic moment. Hangst led ALPHA, which first trapped antihydrogen atoms, measured their 1S–2S transition to parts in 10^12 and showed that antimatter falls under gravity. Ulmer led BASE, which developed multi-trap methods to measure the antiproton magnetic moment to parts per billion and to compare the proton and antiproton charge-to-mass ratios to 16 parts per trillion. Together they are the most stringent direct tests of CPT symmetry with baryons and antiatoms, the product of decades of exceptional instrumentation.
